top_story: Iran is staging Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s posthumous transition with unusual deliberation, moving from broad signaling on 10 June to a fixed funeral sequence from Tehran on 4 July to burial in Mashhad on 9 July, an effort to project continuity and control after months of uncertainty. That choreography unfolds as Washington and Tehran send contradictory signals on ending their war: talk of a possible deal intensified before renewed military action near the Strait of Hormuz on 13 June undercut confidence and exposed how easily escalation can outrun diplomacy. Across the region, Syria’s unresolved file of enforced disappearances remains a standing indictment of state violence, with families still trapped between grief and political impunity rather than postwar closure. The broader picture is of governments trying to manage legitimacy through ceremony or negotiation while ordinary people continue to absorb the costs of conflict, opacity, and deferred justice.
